sections.bio:
I am a 2D/3D Motion Designer with 3+ years of experience creating visually engaging motion graphics and animations for advertising, film, television, and digital platforms.

My work focuses on transforming ideas into clear, impactful visual stories through motion. I have contributed to TV commercials, brand films, social media campaigns, and promotional videos, ensuring each project aligns with brand identity, communication goals, and audience behavior.

I work comfortably across both 2D and 3D pipelines, using tools such as After Effects, Cinema 4D, Blender, Photoshop, Illustrator, and Premiere Pro. From concept development to final delivery, I balance creative exploration with technical accuracy to produce high-quality results.

What I Bring:

Motion design and animation for advertising and brand-led campaigns

Custom 3D models and animations for films, ads, and digital content

High-performing motion graphics and edited videos for social media platforms

Collaboration with designers, marketers, and production teams

Strong attention to detail, timelines, and visual consistency

I enjoy working in environments where creativity meets strategy, and where motion design is used not just for aesthetics, but for communication and impact.

Open to roles in motion graphics, 3D animation, and visual design. :)

posts.text:
If you want to emphasize “I learned” rather than sounding like an expert, I’d make it more personal and humble:
I used to think payments were simple.
Working in fintech taught me otherwise.
One of the most interesting things I’ve recently learned at Transact Bridge is how a Merchant of Record (MoR) works.
Before this, I mostly thought of payments as:
Customer → Payment Gateway → Business
But I learned there’s a lot more happening behind a successful international transaction.
A Merchant of Record can handle responsibilities such as:
→ Payment processing
→ Tax calculation & collection
→ Invoicing
→ Refunds & chargebacks
→ Compliance
→ Local payment methods
→ Settlements


As a designer, this changed the way I look at payment experiences.
A checkout screen may look simple, but behind that interface are complex systems, regulations, business rules, and customer expectations.
That made me realize something:

Good design isn’t just about making an interface look simple.
It’s about understanding the complexity behind it and making that complexity feel simple for the user.

At Transact Bridge, I’m getting the opportunity to learn how payments, tax, compliance, and global expansion come together.

And honestly, there’s a lot more behind a simple “Pay Now” button than I realized.
Still learning. Still designing. Still curious. 🚀


#MerchantOfRecord #ProductDesign #UXDesign #Fintech #Payments #GlobalExpansion #CrossBorderPayments #DesignThinking #Designer #Learning  #linkedin #usa #us #Mor

Most designers add more elements when a design feels weak.

The better approach?
Remove distractions instead.
By combining a frosted glass effect with masking, you guide the viewer's attention without adding visual noise.

Here's why it works: 

✅ Creates a clear focal point
✅ Improves visual hierarchy
✅ Makes the layout feel more premium
✅ Keeps the composition clean and intentional

Remember:
The best design isn't the one with more elements. It's the one that makes users know exactly where to look.

Have you used this technique in your UI or social media designs?

Creative agencies aren't being acquired because they're big. They're being acquired because they're different.
Nikhil Kamath's WTF has acquired BTG (By The Gram)—its second investment in a founder-led creative agency.
The interesting part?
BTG's founders keep full creative and operational control.
That says a lot about where the market is heading.
The next generation of agencies won't win by offering more services. They'll win by building: 
• A unique point of view
 • Deep cultural intelligence
 • Founder-led execution
 • Long-term brand partnerships
Capital can help you scale.
But your creative identity is what makes you valuable.
For founders, agencies, and marketers, this is a reminder:
The strongest competitive advantage isn't size. It's differentiation.
Do you think founder-led creative agencies will outperform traditional network agencies over the next decade?
